1.  26-56371  Recommendation to increase appropriations in the General Fund Group in the City
  Manager Department by $6,000, offset by the Fourth Council District One-Time
  District Priority Funds transferred from the Citywide Activities Department to
  provide support for the following:
  1. $2,800 to Partners of Parks in support of their annual golf festival and “keep
  El Dorado Nature Center open” campaign;
  2. $1,000 to the Historical Society of Long Beach in support of their local
  history preservation efforts;
  3. $500 to Care Closet LBC in support of their continued efforts to provide
  support to the unhoused community;
  4. $500 to Casey Lukowski in support of the Plaza Neighborhood Pumpkin
  Palooza on Josie Avenue;
  5. $1,200 to LBC Hero Squad in support of their 10-year anniversary
  celebration; and

17. 26-56388  Recommendation to request City Manager, in collaboration with City Attorney and
  relevant City departments, to report back to the City Council within 90 days on
  legally permissible and operationally feasible options to strengthen the regulation
  and enforcement of unattached or unhitched trailers, nuisance trailers, oversized
  vehicles, mobile billboard trailers, and trailer-based commercial activity on public
  streets, including potential Long Beach Municipal Code amendments, such as to
  Section 10.18.050 regarding mobile billboard advertising vehicles; traffic
  engineering and location-based parking restrictions; business licensing, permitting,
  and compliance mechanisms; administrative citations and progressive
  enforcement; public nuisance remedies; towing, removal, storage, and release
  protocols.

  A motion was made by Councilwoman Thrash-Ntuk, seconded by
  Councilwoman Kerr, to approve recommendation. The
  motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  8 Zendejas, Allen, Duggan, Supernaw, Kerr, Saro,
  Uranga, Thrash-Ntuk

  1. Bring forward for City Council consideration, within sixty (60) days, an
  ordinance amending the Long Beach Municipal Code that codifies the
  prohibition on the retail sale of nitrous oxide established by Senate Bill 758
  (Chapter 979, Statutes of 2026), conforms to the product and device
  prohibitions established by Senate Bill 936 (Chapter 317, Statutes of 2026),

  Chapter 2.03 under Article 1- Rules of the Council, specifically under the section of
  the Order of Business in order to adopt changes related to City Council
  deliberation, the projection of a publicly displayed timer, and adjourning remarks.

  A motion was made by Councilwoman Allen, seconded by
  Councilmember Duggan, to approve recommendation, as amended, to
  create a council policy to: [1] publicly display a timer during council
  discussion; [2] five (5) minute limitation on announcements per
  speaker with an exception of in memoriams; and [3] request City
  Clerk to make an announcement when somebody leaves the meeting.
